newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Leighton says expects profitable year.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Leighton says expects profitable year.

text.p: Construction group and mining contractor Leighton Holdings Ltd said on Friday it expected good growth for the group to continue in the medium term and that the outlook for 1996/97 was for another strong and profitable year.

"We have hit the ground running in the 1996/97 finnacial year with a combination of new work and contract extensions secured during the first quarter keeping work in hand steady at A$3.3 billion at 30 September," Leighton chairman Tim Besley told the company's annual general meeting.
Besley said the Australian economy remained patchy but in the company's areas of operations the outlook was positive.
In the period leading up to the year 2000, activity in the Australian construction market was forecast to exceed the peak level achieved during the 1980s, he said.

"The Sydney Olympics infrastructure development, a resources sector which is performing well, and the expected increase in activity in the commercial and industrial property sectors, are all areas which should provide good opportunities in Australia," Besley said.
Strong economic growth was forecast in all of the Asian countries in which the group operated.

"Work in hand is at an all-time high and Leighton Asia and Thiess will increase activity levels in 1996/97 as a result," he said. Leighton reported a net profit of A$70.21 million in 1995/96 from A$51.23 million in 1994/95.
Leighton chief executive Wal King told the meeting that with increasing work available in Australia, the group must be firmly focused on controlling costs and optimising resources.
"Asia continues to thrive with ample opportunities for the group," he said.

"Prospects vary in the different countries in which we operate. Our market approach will remain selective and profit driven within the broad footprint established across the region," King said. "Overall the outlook is for another strong and profitable year," he said.
Leighton is 46 owned by Germany's Hochtief Ag.
